hypotheses.justification: rankAtStalk M p is defined as finrank over Localization.AtPrime p of LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M. S is a domain, so 0 ∈ p and every element of p.primeCompl is nonzero, hence a non-zero-divisor: p.primeCompl ≤ nonZeroDivisors S. Two Mathlib lemmas in LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Localization.lean need only this inclusion, with no flatness or finiteness assumption. IsLocalization.rank_eq gives that the rank over the localized ring equals the rank over S. IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq (with f := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap) gives that the localized module has the same rank as M, which is n by hrank. Module.finrank_eq_of_rank_eq then yields finrank = n. The existing proof only uses Flat and FinitePresentation in its first step, Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk plus connectedness, which moves from p to the generic point ⊥. Dropping that step and running the remaining argument directly at p (replace ⊥ by p.asIdeal; prove hle with mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero and p.asIdeal.zero_mem) proves the statement without this hypothesis. Flat and FinitePresentation can even be deleted together.

Same argument as for Module.Flat. In a domain, p.primeCompl ≤ nonZeroDivisors S for every prime p, because 0 ∈ p. Hence IsLocalization.rank_eq and IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq, which assume only this inclusion, give that the rank of LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M over Localization.AtPrime p equals Module.rank S M = n. Module.finrank_eq_of_rank_eq then gives rankAtStalk M p = n. Finite presentation is only used for the local-constancy step (Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk), and that step is not needed. hrank already forces the rank to be finite, so no finiteness of M is needed.
